item.title: Steph Curry has a message for Yaxel Lendeborg after Luka Doncic drama
item.description: Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images Stephen Curry is backing his Golden State Warriors rookie after the Luka Doncic drama. The Lakers dominated the Warriors 127-105, blowing the game open in the second half. Luka Doncic led the charge for L.A. with 28 points, while Stephen Curry paced Golden State with 23. Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg chipped in 12 points in his debut, but the real drama involved him and Doncic. The two exchanged nonstop trash talk during a tight second quarter, culminating in a technical foul for Lendeborg. Afterward, the rookie admitted he lost respect for Doncic over his constant referee complaints, while Luka claimed the chatter only fueled his performance. Steph Curry defends Yaxel Lendeborg’s actions vs Lakers Steph Curry loved seeing rookie Yaxel Lendeborg bring that fire against Luka Doncic . Instead of telling him to tone it down, Steph backed his confidence completely, pointing out that talking trash just means you have to show up and back it up, which is what real competition is all about. Speaking to the media, he said: “I love confidence, I love that care and passion. From what I’ve seen from him, it’s about just playing basketball. It’s not about anything else. He’s setting the table for himself to have to show up. I like the nature of the game, whether you do it in between your ears or you let it out.” Seeing Yaxel Lendeborg bring that total lack of fear onto the big stage is huge for the Warriors. You love seeing a rookie try to set a physical tone and make a name for himself right out of the gate. But he’s about to learn the hard way that the league’s top guys actually feed off that noise, it just gives them extra motivation to embarrass you. Wanting to prove you belong is fine, but poking the bear early usually backfires. At this level, the absolute best message you can send is just letting your game speak for itself. item.title: Zachary Athekame to see out Lyon loan, despite AC Milan’s recall interest
item.description: Zachary Athekame to see out Lyon loan, despite AC Milan’s recall interest Zachary Athekame (21) has enjoyed an excellent start to life at Olympique Lyonnais. The Switzerland international joined over the summer on a season-long loan from AC Milan. The Italian club weren’t necessarily keen to include a buy option in that deal and it has been clear to see why. Brought in to replace Ainsley Maitland-Niles, who would later go on to join Everton, Athekame has quickly become a key player under Paulo Fonseca. In just nine games in all competitions, he has already scored twice and registered three assists. Unlike many attacking modern full-backs, he has also been very tidy defensively. AC Milan were set to welcome him back to the San Siro at the end of the season in any case, given that no buy option was included in the deal. However, RMC Sport understands that the Italian giants held an interest in bringing the right-back back early. Despite that, Athekame is set to see out the season at Lyon, the publication adds. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: 'A number of players playing for their careers': Simon Katich blasts batting approach as Australia fight to save 2nd Test
item.description: Australia are under pressure in the second Test against South Africa, with former batter Simon Katich warning that several players could be fighting to save their places in the team. Marnus Labuschagne, Nic Maddinson and Beau Webster have struggled in the match, leaving Australia with plenty to prove on the final day in Gqeberha. Australia were 156/4 at the end of Day 4 after being asked to follow on, still trailing South Africa by 170 runs. Labuschagne scored 39 before throwing away his wicket with an attacking shot against spinner Simon Harmer. Despite getting starts in recent matches, the batter has struggled to convert them into big scores. Katich questioned Labuschagne’s decision to play an aggressive shot when Australia were trying to save the match. "There are a number of players playing for their careers in this innings," Katich said on SEN radio. He added, "Only he knows what was going through his mind when he tried to take Harmer down the ground, against the breeze, when Australia are trying to play for a draw." Katich also questioned how selectors would view the dismissal, pointing out that Labuschagne had received several opportunities over the years. Labuschagne under pressure as Australia fight back Australia head coach Andrew McDonald was also disappointed with Labuschagne’s latest failure. The 32-year-old has not scored a Test century since July 2023 and continues to struggle to turn promising starts into substantial innings. "I feel like I am on repeat" McDonald said, reflecting on Labuschagne’s repeated scores in the 30s. He added that Australia had built a useful partnership and were beginning to recover before Labuschagne’s dismissal. "When you do that hard work, you've got to cash in, and unfortunately, that wasn't to be the case for Marn. We were disappointed, and he will be too," the coach said. South Africa close in as pressure mounts Australia lead the three-match series 1-0 after winning the first Test at Kingsmead by 214 runs. However, South Africa have fought back strongly in Gqeberha, declaring at 425/9 before dismissing Australia for just 99 in their first innings. Rain limited play during the first two days, but South Africa have put themselves in a strong position to win the match. Travis Head, unbeaten on 87, and nightwatchman Scott Boland will resume Australia's innings on the final day. Australia's team management could face further scrutiny if the visitors lose, particularly after Nathan Lyon's omission from the playing XI drew criticism. 135113570

item.title: “I Want to Help Him Get MVP”: Trae Young Makes Defying Statement on Anthony Davis After Star’s Historic Wizards Debut
item.description: Trae Young, Anthony Davis © X/ @WashWizards Trae Young has high expectations for new co-star Anthony Davis following their exceptional performance in the Washington Wizards’ season opener on Wednesday. Both stars tallied double-doubles – Young scored 20 points and dished 13 assists, while Davis scored 34 and grabbed 12 rebounds, shooting 55.0%. According to the NBA , Davis became the first player in Wizards history to record a 30-point double-double on debut. He also tied Antawn Jamison’s record for most points by a Wizards player in a franchise debut. Young and Davis connected on only one field goal, but their partnership also seemed solid beyond the box score. After the game, Young said he wasn’t surprised by Davis’ explosion and wanted to help him win MVP. “I wasn’t surprised by what he did tonight,” Young said via Bijan Todd’s X. “I don’t want to put too much pressure on him, but for me, having a guy like that, I want to help him get MVP.” An MVP accolade is one of the major things missing from Davis’ resume. Despite having exceptional seasons in the past, voters have overlooked him. At 33, given Davis’ health issues over the past couple of years, not many would pick him to win the award. However, if he consistently delivers performances as he did on opening night, he could at least find himself involved in those conversations. For now, the Wizards fans already consider him an MVP. The crowd serenaded him with MVP chants after eight minutes of play. The Wizards won 128-116. It was the first time they had a record over .500 since Nov. 28, 2022. Anthony Davis lauds crowd and hands strays to Wizards over previous years’ struggles to fill arenas Anthony Davis appreciated the Wizards fans for turning out at Capital One Arena. It was the loudest it has been in years, with Washington adding stars like Davis and Trae Young to run the show. Davis credited the fans for fueling the Wizards’ motivation to win on opening night. “I’d like it to be a little more packed in there, but the crowd was great; they were into it, got us over the hump,” he said via Bijan Todd’s X. Davis then took a hilarious shot at the Wizards’ struggles to fill up arenas last year, saying: “Even when I was here last year, very first home game. It was like, ‘Dress Like a Seat Night’ in here.” The Wizards had been mired at the bottom of the standings every year since their last playoff appearance in 2021. They struggled to attract stars after trading Russell Westbrook to the Lakers the same year. Two years later, Washington moved on from Bradley Beal, further depleting the team’s star depth. However, the Wizards’ front office made drastic changes, trading for All-Star-caliber talents like Trae Young and Anthony Davis at the last deadline when their value was at its lowest. Washington’s fortunes improved further after it won the 2026 draft lottery and landed AJ Dybantsa with the first pick. item.title: Fire Deion Sanders? Why Big 12 teams should want Coach Prime to stay at Colorado
item.description: STILLWATER — Growing up in the Texas Panhandle, Eric Morris watched a lot of Deion Sanders ’ games. But it wasn’t necessarily Prime Time's days with the Dallas Cowboys that the Oklahoma State football coach remembers most. Rather, it was Deion’s time with the Atlanta Braves that is clearest. “When I was young, you always watched the Cubs and the Braves because that was what was on TV at my house back in the day,” Morris said of the national broadcasts from WGN in Chicago and TBS in Atlanta. “So, weirdly, you become attached to those teams that you have no affiliation with because that’s what’s on.” Morris couldn’t help being impressed with Sanders. “One of those unicorns in sports that can do a variety of things,” he said. More: OSU football coach Eric Morris believes Deion Sanders, Colorado best '2-win team' in nation Now, of course, Sanders is doing something else in sports, though the results haven’t been nearly as flashy as his playing days were. Coach Prime is in the midst of his fourth season as the head coach at Colorado , but as he and the Buffs travel to OSU this weekend, it’s safe to assume Sanders is coaching for his job during this back half of the season. The Buffs have just two wins this season and are on a four-game losing streak, and that comes on the heels of a 4-8 record a year ago. Overall, Sanders has a record of 19-24 in Boulder. item.title: See how 20 former CSU football players are faring in college football
item.description: Roster change is the biggest constant in college football right now. Players frequently play for multiple programs in a college football career. That's especially the case for those who go through a coaching change in their career, as happened at CSU in 2025 as the Rams went from Jay Norvell to Jim Mora. There are plenty of former Rams still playing in FBS after leaving Colorado State . Here's a look at 20 former Rams who are still playing college football and how they're faring in 2026. Brayden Fowler-Nicolosi, Michigan The quarterback played 31 career games with the Rams and threw for nearly 7,000 career yards but struggled for consistency. He left CSU's program in the middle of 2025 and then transferred to Michigan. The Wolverines have benched former starter Bryce Underwood, but freshman Tommy Carr will start in his place. Fowler-Nicolosi is the third-string quarterback and has not appeared in any games this season. Jackson Brousseau, Cal Brousseau took over for Fowler-Nicolosi at QB during the 2025 season and threw for 1,354 yards and nine touchdowns in nine games played. He transferred to Cal and began the season as a backup but has found himself on the field amid injuries and inconsistency for Cal. Brousseau started last week for Cal but was benched late in the game and a starter for this week has not been announced. Brousseau has completed 62.5% (75-120) of his passes for 701 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions this season. Owen Long, Arizona State The linebacker led the nation in tackles in 2025 at CSU with 151. Long transferred to Arizona State and he's currently tied for 22nd in FBS with 54 tackles. He also has a fumble forced, fumble recovered and an interception this season. He'll return to Fort Collins Oct. 24 to face the Rams as a member of Pac-12 foe San Diego State. Kinnard has 81 carries for 432 yards (5.3 per carry) and a touchdown in six games so far this season. item.title: One painful stat that is haunting the Bengals offense
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off their bye week as they get geared up for a date with the Baltimore Ravens in Maryland. Sitting at 3-2 on the season, they have some ground to make up as the AFC North continues to be jumbled up in terms of the standings. A win on Sunday would help propel them forward, but to do that, they need the running game to step up. So far this season, the Bengals have struggled to get rolling on the ground, especially running back Chase Brown. Expected to have a big year, Brown has struggled to find the explosive play. That is where this one painful stat really makes your heart hurt some. Brown has the most touches this season without a gain of 15+ yards at 95. The second closest is Kendre Miller at 55. Most touches this season without a gain of 15+ yards: 1. Chase Brown (95!) … 2. Kendre Miller (55) 3. Kaelon Black (47) 4. George Holani (42) 5. Najee Harrison (32) — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) October 20, 2026 With plenty of season left, let’s hope Sunday is the perfect day for Brown to find that explosive play and really help open up Joe Burrow and the play-action game. If so, this team becomes even more dangerous on offense.

item.title: Jacob Bridgeman’s full speech at President Trump’s rally in South Carolina
item.description: Photo by Kent NISHIMURA / AFP via Getty Images President Donald Trump seems to be part of the fabric of Team USA golf. Trump was on the first tee at Bethpage Black for last year’s Ryder Cup, walking out with Bryson DeChambeau and acknowledging all of the players before they started their rounds. He was also at the Presidents Cup on Sunday, presenting the trophy to Team USA and receiving credit for the team’s win from captain Brandt Snedeker after the event. Jacob Bridgeman was a Presidents Cup rookie this year, and he recently spoke at a Trump rally in South Carolina. What Jacob Bridgeman said at a Donald Trump rally in South Carolina Bridgeman appeared on stage with President Trump at his home in South Carolina, and thanked him for his appearance at the Presidents Cup where he made his debut. The 26-year-old said, “Hey South Carolina, it is a great honour to be here with you guys in South Carolina, my home state, where I was born and raised. “I went to Chapman High School in Spartanburg, South Carolina, I live in Greenville now. I attended the best university in the state. “I thank the President Donald Trump for having me here. It has been great to get to know him and to have him at the Presidents Cup, watching us having a pretty historic comeback on Sunday. “And thank you to my captain Brandt Snedeker. He had some good remarks for us after the round and the tournament for our President here. “I thought I would be here with you guys. I am glad to represent one of the best states in the country. I travel a lot, I travel 25 to 30 weeks a year, and every time I come home it feels like at home and there is no place I would rather be. “Thank you to everyone who lives in this great state and thank you for making it what it is and thank you to the President for having me.” Giving credit to the President seems to be a trend that’s developed over the last couple of seasons, so don’t be surprised to see him show up in Ireland for next year’s Ryder Cup. item.title: PSG look to extend Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s contract, despite ACL injury
item.description: PSG look to extend Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s contract, despite ACL injury Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (25) may have sustained an ACL injury on Tuesday, but that has not changed Paris Saint-Germain’s plans to extend his contract, as per a report from RMC Sport. Kvaratskhelia, a nominee for this season’s Ballon d’Or award, was a key figure in PSG’s successful attempt to defend their UEFA Champions League title last season. If Les Parisiens are to make it three in a row, they will have to do it largely without the Georgia international. He sustained an ACL injury during the 4-2 win over Barcelona on Tuesday. He will undergo his an operation in the coming days and is expected to miss the majority, if not the entirety, of the season. Prior to that blow, Kvaratskhelia was locked in contract extension talks with PSG. His current deal at the Parc des Princes runs until 2029. This week’s news has not changed PSG’s plans. The French club are looking to extend the winger’s deal until 2032. They want to make him one of the top earners at the club. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Barcelona summer signing’s impressive record vs Real Madrid offers club a Clasico advantage
item.description: Barcelona summer signing’s impressive record vs Real Madrid offers club a Clasico advantage Barcelona forward Gabriel Jesus could have an important role to play in the Clasico on Sunday, even if it is off the bench. His excellent record against Los Blancos could provide another reason for optimism ahead of the showdown at the Spotify Camp Nou. According to Mundo Deportivo , Jesus has historically performed very well against Real Madrid while playing for his former club. Gabriel Jesus has repeatedly punished Real Madrid The 29-year-old has faced Madrid four times, all during his Manchester City career in the Champions League, recording three victories and one defeat. More impressively, he contributed three goals and one assist across those encounters. His first appearance came in February 2020, when Pep Guardiola deployed him on the left wing at the Santiago Bernabeu. Gabriel Jesus did an excellent job for Manchester City against Real Madrid. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) Jesus scored City’s equaliser in a 2-1 victory and troubled Real Madrid’s defence throughout the match. He was equally influential in the return leg, dispossessing Raphael Varane to create Raheem Sterling’s opener before scoring the winner himself. The Brazilian struck again in the 2021-22 Champions League semi-final first leg, scoring during City’s thrilling 4-3 victory. item.title: Angel Reese makes unprecedented WNBA history with performance in Finals through three games
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese is on a fast track to win WNBA Finals MVP based on her performances through the first three games of their series against the Golden State Valkyries. Reese put up 21 points and 12 rebounds in a 97-71 Game 3 win for the Dream, giving Atlanta a 2-1 series lead in the 2026 WNBA Finals against the vaunted Valkyries. This was Reese’s third straight double-double in the series, a feat that meant she set several new WNBA records with her stat line. Angel Reese’s double-doubles make WNBA history amid Finals series Reese dropped 14 points and 12 rebounds in Game 1 before putting up 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2. Her 21 points and 12 rebounds in Game 3 mean she is the first player in league history to drop three consecutive triple-doubles in her first three games in the Finals. She also became the youngest player in league history to drop three consecutive triple-doubles in the Finals, breaking A’ja Wilson’s record. Reese is averaging 21.7 points, 13.3 rebounds and 2.0 steals during this series, leading both teams in scoring as well as rebounding. Her status as the Defensive Player of the Year is also shining through as she is locking down the Valkyries as arguably the best defensive player in this series. While Reese has reliable production from guards like Alisha Grey and Rhyne Howard, it cannot be disputed that Reese is the head of the snake and leading this Dream squad to a strong start. While the Dream still need to win two more games to become champions and for Reese to achieve her dream of winning Finals MVP, they are currently on pace to achieve that goal primarily because of Reese’s historic production to start the series. item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - JUNE 25: The Philadelphia Phillies logo is pictured on a hat during the game against the Detroit Tigers at Comerica Park on June 25, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) Getty Images The Philadelphia Phillies have several important roster decisions to make this winter as they look to build a more dependable team for another postseason run. While questions about the lineup will demand plenty of attention, the bullpen could be one of the organization’s most pressing priorities after the relief corps struggled to provide consistent bridge options late in the season. The problem became especially apparent during September and the playoffs. “As a dreadful September unfolded and the Wild Card Series arrived, the Philadelphia Phillies had few trusted relievers they could turn to,” Charlotte Varnes and Matt Gelb wrote for The Athletic . “Jhoan Duran to close games, perhaps Alex McFarlane as the setup man. Jose Alvarado or Tim Mayza, perhaps, if they needed a lefty. The rest of the relief corps fell further down the trust tree, whether because of injury or ineffectiveness.” That uncertainty gives Philadelphia a reason to explore both external additions and internal options for new relief arms. item.title: Top-10 recruit Reese Alston trending away from Kentucky as college decision nears
item.description: As Kentucky Basketball fans wait to see when Mark Pope will land his next commitment in the class of 2027, one highly touted recruit appears to be nearing a decision. According to Joe Tipton of On3, 5-star point guard and top-10 recruit Reese Alston is set to make his college decision soon. Alston stands 6-foot-2 and weighs 175 pounds. He is ranked No. 9 nationally, the No. 3 point guard in the class and the No. 1 overall player in Texas. Alston initially included seven schools on his list, but he made visits to only five: Louisville, Wichita State, LSU, Tennessee, and Kentucky. Pope and his staff managed to get Alston on campus for an official visit that caught many by surprise. However, that visit does not appear to have significantly changed his recruitment, as Alston still seems to be deciding between LSU and Louisville, according to Tipton. One positive for Kentucky is that its backcourt remains in a strong position with Zoom Diallo, Alex Wilkins, and Mason Williams all having plenty of eligibility remaining. The Wildcats may not necessarily need to add another guard, provided their current players continue to develop and perform at a high level. For now, Kentucky fans may have to keep waiting for the program’s next commitment in the 2027 class. The Wildcats have just one pledge so far: five-star small forward Ryan Hampton.

item.title: How does Brad Underwood stack up against college basketball’s elite?
item.description: Illinois head coach Brad Underwood joined the Illini in 2017 and faced criticism from some Illinois fans for failing to make a deep run in the NCAA Tournament during his first few seasons. It took him three seasons to lead the Illini back to the Big Dance, but he has since guided the program to an Elite Eight and a Final Four. Underwood silenced his critics by leading Illinois to its first Final Four since 2005 and winning 20 or more games for the seventh consecutive season. He has established himself as one of the best coaches in college basketball and will look to further cement his legacy by leading Illinois to another Final Four this season. item.title: Bromley part company with Woodman after five years
item.description: Andy Woodman won 123 of his 289 games in charge of Bromley, a win percentage of 42.6 [Getty Images] Long-standing Bromley manager Andy Woodman has left the League One club following the mutual termination of his contract. Woodman joined Bromley in 2021 in his first managerial role and oversaw the most successful period in the club's history, winning three trophies in guiding them into the Football League for the first time in their history. Bromley lifted the League Two title in May this year to secure a second successive promotion, with Woodman named the division's manager of the year for 2025-26. But the Ravens have found life in the third tier challenging as they lie 23rd, just one point above Wigan Athletic on the bottom. They have won just two of their 10 league games this season and conceded an EFL-high 25 goals. Assistant manager Byron Webster will take charge of first-team affairs on an interim basis with Peterborough United the visitors to Hayes Lane on Saturday (15:00 BST). Bromley owner and chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves said Woodman had been "fundamental" in helping the club reach new heights. "On a personal note, Andy has been a pleasure to work with, and I wish him all the best for the future," Stanton-Gleaves added. Woodman's five years and seven months in charge of Bromley was the third-longest spell across the 92 clubs in the Premier League and EFL, behind only Arsenal's Mikel Arteta and Nigel Clough of Mansfield. item.title: Martina Navratilova Raises Questions After Hunter Schafer Reveals She Underwent Bottom Surgery at 27
item.description: Martina Navratilova © Imagn images Martina Navratilova reacted pointedly after Euphoria actor Hunter Schafer revealed she underwent bottom surgery. Schafer admitted to undergoing gender-affirming surgery last December. Speaking to Elle magazine, the 27-year-old revealed that she underwent lower body surgery that changes a person’s genitals to better align with their gender identity. She also reflected on her evolving understanding of her gender identity. In the interview, Schafer admitted that she had previously had a more flexible understanding of her gender identity. However, over time, she was sure of identifying as a woman and decided that gender-affirming surgery was the right choice for her. “I just had bottom surgery in December, which was amazing, and I love it so much,” Schafer said while revealing the surgery. “I’m a woman. I’m a girl,” she added. Martina Navratilova took a jab at her, writing: “A 27-year-old girl? Who knew?” Schafer will next be seen alongside Michelle Yeoh in the Amazon miniseries Blade Runner 2099. Martina Navratilova reacts to WNBA clarifying statement on ‘Women’ definition Martina Navratilova recently reacted to the WNBA’s clarification on the definition of “women” amid ongoing debate about transgender athletes’ participation in the league. Indiana Rep. Marlin Stutzman demanded a definition from WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert after ex-NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White were declared ineligible to enter the 2027 WNBA draft. Engelbert responded to Stutzman, while highlighting the league’s definition of “women.” The letter stated that only biological women are eligible to compete in the league, and that Freedom and White are both men. “With respect to your questions regarding eligibility, only women are eligible to play in the WNBA, and the individuals you cite in your letter are both men,” the letter read. “The WNBA will continue its efforts to ensure the safety, fair treatment, and well-being of our players and personnel, including working to address the significant amount of hate and vitriol directed at WNBA players online and on social media.” Martina Navratilova appreciated the WNBA’s clarification but questioned how the league would differentiate between someone who is transgender and someone pretending to be one. “Good to know… but how do you tell the real trans from not real trans? Or just no trans, period? What say you @WNBA” Martina Navratilova also expressed her dissent after XX-XY Athletics founder Jennifer Sey received derogatory remarks from Valkyries fans during the WNBA Finals. item.title: Alex Marquez: Decision to travel to Qatar should not be made right now
item.description: Motorsport photo With two weeks to go until the Qatar Grand Prix, MotoGP riders continue to express their misgivings about the championship's intention to race in a region affected by an armed conflict. While some riders, such as Marc Marquez, avoided talking about the issue, most subscribed to the argument that 'if MotoGP decides to go to Qatar, it will be because safety is guaranteed'. Ahead of this weekend's Australian Grand Prix, the championship's officials have scheduled a meeting with the riders on Thursday to inform them that the Qatar race is going ahead and that they will to guarantee their safety at the event. It's a decision that Gresini's Alex Marquez considers premature, saying he would prefer if a definitive call isn't made until later. "Every day, [the situation] changes and every day it looks worse, that's how it is," the Spaniard said on Thursday. "The championship tells us that everything is under control, but I think nobody has a situation like that under control; it's quite complex. "From one day to the next, everything can change a lot, and I think it's not a decision they should make now. They should be realistic and wait for the next few days. Start action Start action "I'm aware there is a lot of money at stake, for sure, and it's logical that MotoGP wants that money, but we also have to think about everyone's health. They have to be careful because a lot of people will go there." Meanwhile, championship leader Jorge Martin maintained a diplomatic stance on the matter, echoing comments from some other riders that they had faith in MotoGP. "I want to go to Qatar because the circuit is incredible, and I believe in the championship and in what those who manage it decide," said the Aprilia rider. "Nobody has said we're not going. It's just another race. If we go, great; if not, that's fine too. If the organisers decide we can go, it'll be because our safety is guaranteed." item.title: Injured Lawlor to miss Wales' final Nations League games
item.description: Dylan Lawlor has won six caps for Wales [Getty Images] Defender Dylan Lawlor will miss Wales' final two Nations League matches against Norway and Portugal with a hamstring injury. The 20-year-old suffered the setback playing for Cardiff City against Watford earlier this month, having only just returned from a knee issue which kept him out of the start of the season. He has now been ruled out until after November's international break. "It's naturally very disappointing," said Bluebirds head coach Brian Barry-Murphy. "He's put so much work into coming back from his knee injury that he suffered so long ago. "But this gives him a chance to do his rehabilitation properly with no rush and make sure that when he comes back, he's good to go again." Lawlor has not played for Wales since suffering the original problem during the 1-1 draw with Ghana in June. He made his first start of the season at Blackburn on 10 October, before suffering his hamstring issue just three days later. Cardiff can earn points and praise - Barry-Murphy Lawlor surprise over breakthrough season at Cardiff When asked if he regretted playing the defender in Cardiff's games against both Blackburn and Watford after such a long spell out, Barry-Murphy said "a little bit". Speaking prior to Cardiff's Championship match against Birmingham on Saturday, Barry-Murphy revealed Lawlor is expected to be out for around five to six weeks. "Hindsight is an easy thing but he did a really good job against Blackburn," the Irishman added. "We wanted to give him some consistency and we needed him really so we were limited in what options we had. "It is what it is now we have to just move forward." Dylan Lawlor has made just three appearances for Cardiff City this season [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales play Norway in Oslo on 14 November before hosting Portugal in Cardiff three days later. Craig Bellamy's team still have a chance of avoiding relegation from League A and securing a Euro 2028 qualification seedings boost. "I think the positive is that his knee hasn't been pain free since the Ghana game for Wales," Barry-Murphy added. "So even though when he came back against Blackburn he still had some pain in it and in the game against Watford where he got injured he wasn't totally pain-free or comfortable. "So this five or six week period, however long it is, gives us a chance to really protect his knee, strengthen it and make sure that when he does come back from this and his hamstring injury that he now has, he's in a very positive position to be fit for the remainder of the season." item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) returns to the field in a sling during the NCAA football game against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium Stadium in Bloomington, Ind. on Oct. 17, 2026. The Ohio State Buckeyes have a tough road in front of them. The Buckeyes managed to hold on for a win against the Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday, but it was a costly victory, with star quarterback Julian Sayin forced out of the game with an injury to his throwing arm. This week, the Ohio State head coach gave an update on Sayin, and it’s wasn’t what Buckeyes fans wanted to hear. “We’re not gonna put any timeline for his injury, but he is out indefinitely,” Day said, via Dan Hope of Eleven Warriors. Now, the Buckeyes are turning to freshman Luke Fahey, and the hope is that he can pull off what Cardale Jones did and lead them to a title as a backup. Josh Pate, however, doesn’t see that in the cards. “I think they’ll lose. I think they’ll lose at least three games, and I think they’ll miss the playoff. I don’t think they’ll be in the postseason,” Pate said on the Rich Eisen Show. “Dang. I think they’ll be a 9-3 team, really good defense. And if they make it, it’ll be because of defense, because that’s another thing, Rich. I keep going back to this— Julian Sayan, before he got hurt, was not performing phenomenally. “I think they’ll lose 3 games and miss the playoffs.” – Josh Pate Post it all over the Woody. @ryandaytime @OhioStateFB https://t.co/xbkZea9I81 — Buckeye HQ (@RealisticBuck) October 21, 2026 “You watched that Indiana game like I did. Neither of those quarterbacks were really dealing. Now they’re facing two really good defenses, but you know, Trinidad Chambliss is going to face a good defense this weekend. I guarantee you he still has really good numbers.” What about the run game? Pate then pointed to other highly touted quarterbacks around the nation who aren’t living up to expectations as an example of what we might see under Fahey and the Buckeyes moving forward. “The point I was going to make is: look at all these quarterbacks around here. item.title: Julian Nagelsmann open to Man Utd job as pressure mounts on Michael Carrick
item.description: Julian Nagelsmann open to Man Utd job as pressure mounts on Michael Carrick Julian Nagelsmann would be receptive to becoming Manchester United manager if the club decide to dismiss Michael Carrick following their disastrous start to the season. According to The Telegraph , the former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach is among the leading candidates United could consider should they make another managerial change. The 39-year-old is currently available after leaving his position with Germany following their disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign. Nagelsmann is understood to be interested in managing in the Premier League and would be willing to discuss the opportunity with United. However, no formal approach has been confirmed, with the club continuing to support Carrick despite growing concerns over results and performances. United have won just twice in 11 matches across all competitions this season and are without a victory in their last seven outings. Wednesday’s humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como intensified scrutiny of Carrick, whose tactical approach has also attracted criticism. Captain Bruno Fernandes questioned the team’s response to pressure after the defeat, calling for greater bravery from his teammates. The result has prompted renewed consideration of potential managerial alternatives, although Carrick remains in charge ahead of Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth. Nagelsmann’s previous relationship with United recruitment director Christopher Vivell could strengthen his candidacy. The pair worked together at RB Leipzig, while Vivell was also at Chelsea when the London club considered appointing Nagelsmann in 2023. Nevertheless, the German reportedly has reservations about recruitment structures and would likely seek assurances regarding United’s sporting operations before accepting any offer. Nagelsmann previously attracted interest from Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur, while his experience with Bayern and Germany makes him an established candidate. He was also spotted at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday watching Bayern’s 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal. Brighton & Hove Albion manager Fabian Hurzeler is another figure admired by United, although his long-term contract could complicate any approach. Former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe and Aston Villa’s Unai Emery are also among the names under consideration. Carrick signed a two-year contract during the summer after guiding United into the Champions League following Ruben Amorim’s dismissal. However, the former midfielder now faces increasing pressure to reverse the club’s decline. Sunday’s encounter with Bournemouth could prove particularly significant, with another disappointing result potentially forcing United’s hierarchy to reconsider their position. For now, Nagelsmann remains a potential replacement rather than the subject of confirmed negotiations.

item.title: Why Man United didn’t let Bruno Fernandes speak to the media in Italian after Como loss
item.description: Why Man United didn’t let Bruno Fernandes speak to the media in Italian after Como loss Sky Sport Italia’s pitchside reporter Pierluigi Bagnulo reveals that Manchester United’s press office didn’t let Bruno Fernandes speak Italian in a post-match interview after a 4-1 loss to Como, ‘fearing they wouldn’t understand his words.’ Como crushed Manchester United 4-1 in a Champions League match played at the Stadio Sinigaglia on Wednesday. Cesc Fabregas’ team delivered a dominant performance , as the result suggests, once again highlighting Manchester United’s fragility and putting further pressure on their boss, Michael Carrick. ITALY – OCTOBER 21: Bruno Fernandes and Matthijs de Ligt of Manchester United react during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Sky Sport Italia journalist Pierluigi Bagnulo, who covered the match as a pitchside reporter in Como last night, reflected on the Red Devils’ struggles with a social media post. “It was almost disturbing to see how disjointed a team that has ‘United’ in its name is,” he wrote. “I witnessed the caption of the actual state of Manchester United in four episodes happening in the space of ten minutes.” ITALY – OCTOBER 21: Michael Carrick, Manager of Manchester United, reacts after during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The list began with “Carrick ignoring his players at the final whistle, going straight to the fans to apologise.” The journalist continued, adding that Bruno Fernandes was not allowed to answer Sky Sport Italia’s questions in Italian. The Portuguese midfielder spent many years in Italy early in his career, playing for Novara, Sampdoria and Udinese and speaks perfect Italian. “The press office prevented Bruno Fernandes from speaking in Italian for a post-match interview, fearing they wouldn’t understand his words,” Bagnulo said. LEEDS, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 18: Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United applauds the fans following the team’s draw in the Premier League 2026/27 match between Leeds United and Manchester United at Elland Road on October 18, 2026 in Leeds, England. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) “Bruno said that Manchester United must stop thinking about the past; otherwise they’ll never get over this. Carrick (a gentleman for how he behaved after the match) contradicted him a minute later, saying he doesn’t agree at all. “It’s a club that is sadly crumbling hour after hour.” Milan legend Zvonimir Boban, a Sky Sport Italia pundit, criticized both Bruno Fernandes and Manchester United at full time, saying the Red Devils “will not have a present or future at a strong level as long as he [Bruno] is the best player.”

item.title: Former Cambridge goalkeeper Vaughan dies aged 62
item.description: John Vaughan was goalkeeping coach at clubs including Huddersfield Town, Birmingham City and Bradford City [Getty Images] Former Cambridge United, Preston North End and Lincoln City goalkeeper John Vaughan has died aged 62. Vaughan also had spells at Fulham and Charlton Athletic in an 18-year playing career. At Cambridge, he was part of the John Beck-managed side who won back-to-back promotions from Division Four, now League Two, to Division Two, now the Championship, in the 1989-90 and 1990-91 seasons. In a post on X, Huddersfield Town, where Vaughan previously served as a goalkeeping coach, said they were "saddened" by news of his passing. Vaughan also served as a goalkeeping coach at clubs including Birmingham City and Bradford City. In a tribute of their own, the Bantams said that their thoughts were, "with John's family and loved ones at this devastating time". As a player, Vaughan also enjoyed success at Preston, where he was part of the team who won the Third Division title in 1995-96. His 66 league appearances for the Lilywhites ranks only behind the 178 times he represented Cambridge between 1988 and 1993. Vaughan was voted among Cambridge United's all-time greatest team as part of a mural at the Abbey Stadium [Getty Images] All the latest Cambridge United news

item.title: Baker Mayfield Injury Update: Buccaneers QB’s Week 7 Status Revealed
item.description: Baker Mayfield dislocated his thumb during Week 3’s battle against the Minnesota Vikings, and the quarterback could make his return to the field in Week 7. Originally selected with the first-overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft , the Oklahoma product began his career on the bench but quickly earned the starting job as a rookie. After a promising rookie season where he completed 63.8% of his passes for 3,725 yards, 27 touchdowns, and 14 interceptions, the quarterback guided the team to the playoffs and earned a victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers in the Wild Card round. However, this wasn’t enough for him to stick around as Cleveland’s long-term answer. The Browns effectively swapped him for Deshaun Watson and, after short stints with the Carolina Panthers and Los Angeles Rams, Baker Mayfield found a home with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Despite making two Pro Bowls in his first two seasons with the club, Mayfield didn’t play well before the injury and went 0-3 to start the season. Despite their current 1-5 record, Tampa Bay is still in the playoff race, and Mayfield could return to help his team this Sunday. According to the team’s practice report , the quarterback was a full participant, which means he will likely start against the Carolina Panthers. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor Baker Mayfield Injury Update: Buccaneers QB Likely to Return In Week 7 With Baker Mayfield sidelined, the Buccaneers had no choice but to roll with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. The Kansas product did what he could to keep the season afloat but ultimately finished with a 1-2 record and unimpressive stats. Most 1-5 teams normally don’t stand a chance at the playoffs, but the NFC South gives Tampa Bay a realistic shot at meaningful January football. As of this posting, the 3-2 Carolina Panthers sit atop the NFC South, and they’re the only team in the division with a winning record. If Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers defeat the Panthers, they’ll only be 1.5 games out of the division lead with a head-to-head tiebreaker advantage. Seeing as head coach Todd Bowles could lose his job if the team cannot make the postseason, they’ll have every reason to play hard for the rest of the year. Main Photo: Kim Klement – Imagn Images

item.title: Nordic combined sets hopes in Macron for Olympic survival after all
item.description: FILE PHOTO - (L-R) The German combined skiers Julian Schmid, Jenny Nowak, Nathalie Armbruster and Vinzenz Geiger celebrate their silver medal after the combined - team, normal hill/2 x 5/2 x 2.5 km, cross-country skiing of the FIS Ski Jumping World Championships in Trondheim at Granasen Ski Centre. (is associated with: «Nordic combined sets hopes in Macron for Olympic survival after all») Hendrik Schmidt/dpa Nordic combined skiers hope for a final chance to avoid being dropped from the 2030 Winter Olympics programme in the form of French President Emmanuel Macron. German ski federation sporting director Horst Hüttel has said that the sport's Olympic champion Jason Lamy Chappuis and fellow French former biathlon great Martin Fourcade want to lobby for Nordic combined at a meeting with Macron in November. "If there would be a signal from the host nation then that would be another chance," Hüttel said. Nordic combined, which twins ski jumping and cross country skiing, was on the programme of all Winter Olympics from the first edition in 1924 onwards. But it has been dropped by the International Olympic Committee for the 2030 Games in the French Alps. The women have never competed at the Olympics. Hüttel said that a decision is planned for the fourth quarter of 2027 whether Nordic combined can return in 2034. He said that "if we face another rejection then, we will have no further options for elite sport." Former overall women's World Cup champion Nathalie Armbruster said: "We simply don't know anything yet. You feel quite helpless. I've fought so hard, and you get so tired of fighting. We have unbeatable arguments, but you still can't make a difference." An adjustment to the competition structure remains under discussion as a possible rescue measure. One possibility is a more compact schedule, in which the cross country portion could take place just 15 minutes after the last ski jumper has finished. New formats may now be introduced in the World Cup "without testing them beforehand", said Hüttel, adding: "The athletes are ready for anything. If that saves the situation, then they'll do it." Germany coach Eric Frenzel also sees a more compact competition schedule as "the only possible way forward". In view of the uncertain future, three-time Olympic champion Frenzel said that they were "at the mercy of certain committees and decision-makers who sit much higher up".

item.description: NORTH SMITHFIELD – Natasha Jenkins knew the exact number without thinking. The number of years since North Smithfield girls volleyball won a title is on everyone’s mind this season. We've all grown with them, since freshman year. To get them a win for their senior year, and obviously for us, but to get them a win is really an achievement. item.title: Real Madrid find themselves in a turmoil over superstar’s declining form
item.description: Real Madrid find themselves in a turmoil over superstar’s declining form Real Madrid fans were elated after the news of Vinicius Jr.’s contract extension in the summer. The forward was coming on the back of a great World Cup campaign and was one of the club’s better performers during the second half of last season. However, renewing Vinicius’ on a long-term contract and giving him a hefty salary package appears to have backfired this season. Vinicius has been nowhere near his best under the leadership of Jose Mourinho, putting Real Madrid in a delicate situation. Real Madrid in heaps of trouble As reported by journalist Sergio Valentin , Vinicius is grappling with a double challenge. The first concerns his own dip in form, while the second relates to the rise of Yan Diomande . Vinicius has been a shadow of his former self this season. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) For the first time in his Madrid career, the forward finds himself facing real competition for his place, a scenario he is not accustomed to. That new reality has left him in an uncomfortable position, and it is one that has created friction with his manager. A problem for Mourinho and Perez Valentin notes that Jose Mourinho finds himself in a highly sensitive spot, tasked with managing a player who is not delivering the required output yet struggles to accept being benched or substituted during matches. Vinicius won’t be available vs Barcelona.. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Complicating matters further is Vinicius’ standing with the hierarchy. The Brazilian continues to enjoy a special status with president Florentino Perez, who sanctioned a contract extension until 2032 worth a net salary of around €25 million per season. That makes it an enormous investment in a player whose value appears to be declining rapidly. It leaves Madrid caught in an awkward bind, committed financially and politically to a forward who is currently unable to justify either the outlay or his place in the side. With the Clasico on the horizon and Vinicius serving a domestic suspension, the timing of his struggles could hardly be worse. With that in mind, how Mourinho navigates the situation will be interesting as the coach will likely to have take on not only Vinicius himself but also president Perez.

item.title: Real Madrid or Barcelona? Jurgen Klopp chooses 'the better' side for El Clasico as Germany boss admits he DISLIKED Blancos stars
item.description: Jurgen Klopp Lamine Yamal Real Madrid El Clasico - Getty Images Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp has weighed in on the eternal debate between Spain’s two biggest clubs ahead of the upcoming El Clasico clash between Barcelona and Real Madrid. The former Liverpool manager revealed which side he is currently backing to triumph at the Camp Nou while reflecting on his historical feelings toward the rivalry. Klopp's Clasico allegiance revealed Klopp confirmed he will be tuning into the upcoming blockbuster clash between Barcelona and Real Madrid. Speaking during the interval of Bayern Munich’s Champions League encounter with Arsenal , the Germany manager explained that this fixture has been a constant presence throughout his footballing life. Despite the shifting balance of power in Spanish football, Klopp remains heavily invested in the rivalry. He will also be keeping a close eye on German forward Karim Adeyemi, noting the Barcelona star's impressive recent upturn in form over the past few weeks. Past grievances and current favourites FC Barcelona v Real Madrid: Spanish Super Cup The former Liverpool boss admitted that the sheer magnitude of the rivalry means he never misses the occasion. "Of course I’ll watch El Clasico between Barcelona and Real Madrid. I’ve watched this game at every stage of my life," Klopp said, as quoted by Bulinews . Reflecting on his historical loyalties, the Germany manager was candid about why he traditionally backed the Catalan giants, pointing to Real Madrid's historically aggressive tactics as a major turn-off. "In the past, I was more of a Barcelona supporter because I was against the actions of Pepe and other Madrid defenders," he explained. "Today, I support the better team. And looking at things at the moment, that is probably Barcelona." Mixed fortunes for Spain's heavyweights Klopp's assessment arrives as both clubs navigate contrasting European fortunes. Hansi Flick’s Barcelona are reeling from a 4-2 Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain , a match that also saw playmaker Dani Olmo suffer a serious muscle injury . The Spaniard is now sidelined for a month, ruling him out of the pivotal Camp Nou clash. Conversely, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are flying high after dismantling RB Leipzig 4-1 . Kylian Mbappe provided a goal and an assist in the resounding victory. However, Los Blancos must tackle the Catalan giants without suspended star winger Vinicius Junior . Stepping up to the plate FBL-EUR-C1-REAL MADRID-LEIPZIG With Vinicius unavailable for the first Clasico of the campaign, Mourinho faces a significant attacking reshuffle. The Portuguese tactician is expected to rely heavily on Yan Diomande to plug the gap on the flank. The substitute forward staked his claim against Leipzig with a spectacular late volley, taking his recent tally to three goals and one assist in his last four outings. Diomande must now attempt to replicate that devastating form on Spain's biggest stage as Madrid look to prove Klopp wrong

item.title: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
item.description: Title is club’s first-ever since 2023 founding St Louis clubs have won 11 Open Cups all-time Daniel Edelman nets winner in 5-4 win on penalties For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis. The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023. From the beginning, club figures spoke of aims to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties away from home to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
